description: The primary aim of the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge is to build an intuitive, interactive tool or application that allows mission planners, educators, and the public to evaluate and compare potential lunar landing sites by visualizing environmental trade-offs.
summary: Our lunar mission-planning platform incorporates lunar elevation products from the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) aboard NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. These products support the platform’s terrain and elevation visualisations after conversion into web-compatible formats. The platform also integrates NASA/JPL’s Horizons service for solar-system ephemeris calculations intended to support solar-position analysis. Other outputs—including communication geometry, hazard indicators, landing-site comparisons, and power estimates—are project-generated calculations or simplified models and are presented as estimates, not as official NASA mission predictions or certifications.
